questions.q: Choose the one word that can be substituted for: 'A person who walks in sleep'
questions.x: 'Somnambulist' means a person who walks in sleep.

questions.q: Select the antonym of the word 'Meagre'.
questions.x: 'Meagre' is the opposite of 'Ample'. The other options are similar in meaning to 'Meagre'.

questions.q: The officer was accused ____ negligence in handling the files.
questions.x: 'Accused of' is the correct collocation.

questions.q:
Identify the segment of the sentence that contains a grammatical error. If the sentence is correct, choose 'No error'.
Ram is / elder than / his cousin.
questions.x: The error is in part (b): 'elder than'. 'Elder' is not followed by 'than'; use 'older than'.

questions.q: What does the phrase 'To get into hot soup' mean?
questions.x: 'To get into hot soup' means: to get into trouble.

questions.q:
Identify the segment of the sentence that contains a grammatical error. If the sentence is correct, choose 'No error'.
Neither the clerk / nor the officers was / aware of the new circular.
questions.x: The error is in part (b): 'nor the officers was'. With 'neither…nor', the verb agrees with the nearer subject 'officers': 'were aware'.

questions.q: Choose the word that is most nearly SAME in meaning to: QUELL
questions.x: 'Quell' means suppress. 'Provoke' is close to its opposite; the others are unrelated or look-alike words.

questions.q: What does the phrase 'To get cold feet' mean?
o: To become nervous and hesitate before an event
To run away from a fight
questions.x: 'To get cold feet' means: to become nervous and hesitate before an event.

questions.q: Choose the word OPPOSITE in meaning to: SHALLOW
questions.x: 'Shallow' is the opposite of 'Profound'. The other options are similar in meaning to 'Shallow'.

questions.q: Choose the one word that can be substituted for: 'One who is unable to pay debts'
questions.x: 'Insolvent' means one who is unable to pay debts.

questions.q: What does the author consider the most powerful tool of financial inclusion?
questions.x: Answer: 'The mobile phone'. The first sentence says so. The other options either add ideas not found in the passage or contradict it.
questions.p: The mobile phone has become the most powerful tool of financial inclusion. A farmer in a remote village can now receive a subsidy, pay a supplier and check crop prices without travelling to a town. But access is not the same as confidence. Many first-time users fear making mistakes or being cheated, and fraudsters exploit this fear. Digital literacy and simple, local-language interfaces are as important as the network itself.

questions.q: The statement 'access is not the same as confidence' implies that:
o: Everyone with a phone is confident
Having a phone does not ensure that people use digital finance comfortably and safely
questions.x: Answer: 'Having a phone does not ensure that people use digital finance comfortably and safely'. The passage goes on to describe fear of mistakes and fraud. The other options either add ideas not found in the passage or contradict it.
questions.p: The mobile phone has become the most powerful tool of financial inclusion. A farmer in a remote village can now receive a subsidy, pay a supplier and check crop prices without travelling to a town. But access is not the same as confidence. Many first-time users fear making mistakes or being cheated, and fraudsters exploit this fear. Digital literacy and simple, local-language interfaces are as important as the network itself.

questions.q: Gandhi established the Phoenix Settlement and Tolstoy Farm in:
questions.x: Correct answer: South Africa. They were experiments in community living and satyagraha training.

questions.q: Who was the Viceroy of India at the time of the Delhi Durbar of 1911 and the transfer of the capital to Delhi?
questions.x: Lord Hardinge II was Viceroy during the Delhi Durbar of 1911 and the transfer of the capital to Delhi.

questions.q: The Vernacular Press Act was passed under Lord Lytton — this happened in the year:
questions.x: The Vernacular Press Act was passed under Lord Lytton in 1878. Fix this date on your 1857–1947 timeline along with the events immediately before and after it.

questions.q: The 'Subsidiary Alliance' system was devised by:
questions.x: Correct answer: Lord Wellesley. Hyderabad (1798) was the first state to accept it.

questions.q: The 'Justice Party' (South Indian Liberal Federation) was formed in 1916 to represent:
o: Non-Brahmin interests in the Madras Presidency
questions.x: Correct answer: Non-Brahmin interests in the Madras Presidency. It formed governments in Madras under dyarchy.

questions.q:
Consider the following:
Assertion (A): Gandhi suspended the Non-Cooperation Movement in 1922.
Reason (R): Gandhi felt that people had not yet learnt non-violence after the Chauri Chaura violence.
Select the correct answer:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
questions.x: Correct answer: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A. A is true and R is true; R correctly explains A. R explains A.

questions.q: The book 'Why I Am an Atheist' was written by:
questions.x: 'Why I Am an Atheist' was written by Bhagat Singh.

questions.q: In the Ahmedabad mill strike of 1918, Gandhi used which method for the first time in India?
questions.x: Correct answer: Hunger strike. The workers won a 35% wage increase.

questions.q: Sister Nivedita, a disciple of Swami Vivekananda, was originally named:
questions.x: Correct answer: Margaret Elizabeth Noble. Madeleine Slade was Gandhi's follower 'Mirabehn'.

questions.q:
Match the tribal/peasant movement with its leader:
Movement:
A. Munda Ulgulan
B. Santhal Hul (1855)
C. Rampa rebellion (1922–24)
D. Eka movement (1921–22)
Leader:
1. Sidhu and Kanhu
2. Birsa Munda
3. Madari Pasi
4. Alluri Sitarama Raju
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.x:
Correct matching — A (Munda Ulgulan) → 2 (Birsa Munda); B (Santhal Hul (1855)) → 1 (Sidhu and Kanhu); C (Rampa rebellion (1922–24)) → 4 (Alluri Sitarama Raju); D (Eka movement (1921–22)) → 3 (Madari Pasi).
These movements protested against exploitation by landlords, moneylenders and colonial laws.

questions.q: India's men's hockey team won the Asia Cup 2025 at Rajgir (Bihar), defeating:
questions.x: Correct answer: South Korea. The win secured direct qualification for the 2026 FIH World Cup.

questions.q: T. V. Somanathan took over in August 2024 as:
questions.x: The Cabinet Secretary is the head of the civil services.

questions.q: The 16th BRICS Summit in October 2024 was held at:
questions.x: Correct answer: Kazan, Russia. It was the first summit after the 2024 expansion.

questions.q: Which of the following organisations is headquartered in Nairobi?
questions.x: UN Environment Programme is based in Nairobi.

questions.q: NISAR, launched in July 2025 aboard GSLV-F16, is a joint Earth-observation satellite of ISRO and:
questions.x: Correct answer: NASA. It uses dual-band (L- and S-band) synthetic aperture radar.

questions.q: The 'Smart Cities Mission' was launched in:
questions.x: Correct answer: 2015. 100 cities were selected through a challenge process.

questions.q: The first Vande Bharat Express was flagged off in 2019 between:
questions.x: Correct answer: New Delhi and Varanasi. Vande Bharat sleeper versions are being introduced.

questions.q:
Consider the following pairs of exercise and partner country:
1. Yudh Abhyas — USA
2. Dharma Guardian — Japan
3. Mitra Shakti — Sri Lanka
How many of the above pairs are correctly matched?
questions.x:
3 of the 3 listed items satisfy the condition asked.
All three are correctly matched.

questions.q: Kerala was declared India's first 'digitally literate' State in:
questions.x: The 'Digi Keralam' programme trained citizens in basic digital skills.

questions.q: Which day is observed on 24 January?
questions.x: 24 January is National Girl Child Day.

questions.q:
Match the writ with its meaning:
Writ:
A. Habeas corpus
B. Mandamus
C. Certiorari
D. Quo warranto
Meaning:
1. By what authority
2. We command
3. To be certified / informed
4. To have the body (produce a detained person)
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.x:
Correct matching — A (Habeas corpus) → 4 (To have the body (produce a detained person)); B (Mandamus) → 2 (We command); C (Certiorari) → 3 (To be certified / informed); D (Quo warranto) → 1 (By what authority).
Prohibition is the fifth writ, issued to a lower court to stop proceedings beyond jurisdiction.

questions.q: The Constitution (91st Amendment) Act, 2003:
o: Sought to establish the National Judicial Appointments Commission (later struck down)
Limited the size of the Council of Ministers to 15% of the strength of the Lok Sabha/Assembly
Gave constitutional status to Panchayati Raj institutions
Made Sikkim a full-fledged State of the Indian Union
questions.x: The 91st Amendment (2003) limited the size of the Council of Ministers to 15% of the strength of the Lok Sabha/Assembly.

questions.q: Which Article of the Constitution of India provides for: "Elections on the basis of adult suffrage"?
questions.x: This subject is dealt with in Article 326.

questions.q: The Third Schedule of the Constitution contains:
o: Emoluments and allowances of the President, Governors, Judges, CAG and others
Allocation of seats in the Rajya Sabha
Powers, authority and responsibilities of Panchayats (29 subjects)
questions.x: Third Schedule: Forms of oaths and affirmations.

questions.q: The 'Advocate General' of a State is appointed by:
questions.x: Correct answer: The Governor. Article 165; he/she is the highest law officer of the State.

questions.q: Classical language status was granted in October 2024 to which group of languages?
o: Marathi, Pali, Prakrit, Assamese and Bengali
questions.x: Correct answer: Marathi, Pali, Prakrit, Assamese and Bengali. This raised the number of classical languages to eleven.

questions.q: Article 22 of the Constitution of India deals with:
o: Provisions with respect to an Inter-State Council
Protection against arrest and detention in certain cases
questions.x: Article 22: Protection against arrest and detention in certain cases.

questions.q: Which court has the power to issue writs for enforcement of rights other than Fundamental Rights as well?
questions.x: Correct answer: High Courts under Article 226. Article 226 is wider: 'for any other purpose'.

questions.q: Which Article of the Constitution of India provides for: "Promotion of international peace and security"?
questions.x: This subject is dealt with in Article 51.

questions.q: Who presides over a joint sitting of the two Houses of Parliament?
o: The Speaker of the Lok Sabha
questions.x: Correct answer: The Speaker of the Lok Sabha. Article 118(4); in the Speaker's absence the Deputy Speaker presides.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Monetary Policy Committee:
1. It decides the policy repo rate.
2. The Finance Minister chairs its meetings.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is incorrect.
The RBI Governor chairs the MPC; the government nominates three external members.

questions.q: The 'Agricultural Produce Market Committee' (APMC) system regulates:
o: Sale of farm produce in notified markets
questions.x: Correct answer: Sale of farm produce in notified markets. Model APMC Act (2017) and e-NAM aim to reform it.

questions.q: The Unified Payments Interface (UPI) was developed by:
questions.x: Correct answer: National Payments Corporation of India. NPCI launched UPI in 2016.

questions.q: In 2025, India was reported (IMF estimates) to have overtaken which economy to become the fourth largest in nominal GDP terms?
questions.x: According to IMF projections, India's GDP surpassed Japan's in 2025.

questions.q: A depreciation of the rupee against the dollar is likely to:
o: Reduce the cost of foreign debt
questions.x: Correct answer: Make Indian exports cheaper abroad. Exports become competitive; imports and foreign debt costlier.

questions.q: A fixed deposit pays 9% per annum while inflation is 3%. Using the Fisher approximation, the real rate of interest is about:
questions.x:
Fisher approximation: real rate ≈ nominal rate − inflation = 9 − 3 = 6%.
(Exact: (1.09/1.03 − 1) × 100 ≈ 5.83%.)

questions.q: 'Outcome budget' in India focuses on:
o: Measurable outputs and outcomes of expenditure
questions.x: Correct answer: Measurable outputs and outcomes of expenditure. It was introduced in 2005–06.

questions.q: The Open Network for Digital Commerce (ONDC) aims to:
o: Democratise e-commerce through open, interoperable protocols
questions.x: Correct answer: Democratise e-commerce through open, interoperable protocols. It allows buyers and sellers on different platforms to transact.

questions.q: Under the flexible inflation targeting framework, the Government has set the CPI inflation target at:
questions.x: Correct answer: 4% with a tolerance band of ±2%. The target set in 2016 was retained for 2021–26.

questions.q: NABARD's primary role is:
o: Refinancing and development of agriculture and rural sector credit
questions.x: It was set up in 1982 on the recommendation of the Shivaraman Committee.

questions.q: The profits of a firm for the last 4 years were ₹47,000, ₹27,000, ₹26,000, ₹42,000. Goodwill is to be valued at 2 years' purchase of the average profit. Goodwill is:
A partner withdrew ₹3,000 at the beginning of every month during the year. Interest on drawings is charged at 8% p.a. The interest on drawings is:
questions.x:
Total drawings = 12 × 3,000 = ₹36,000.
Average period for monthly drawings made at the beginning of each month = 6.5 months.
Interest = 36,000 × 8% × 6.5/12 = ₹1,560.

questions.q: Life membership fees received by a club are generally:
questions.x: Correct answer: Capitalised (added to the capital fund). Being non-recurring, they are capitalised.

questions.q: Machinery costing ₹2,70,000 is depreciated at 15% per annum on the Written Down Value method. Its book value at the end of 3 years will be:
questions.x:
WDV: depreciation each year is charged on the opening book value.
Book value = Cost × (1 − r)ⁿ = 2,70,000 × (0.85)^3 = ₹1,65,813.75.
(SLM at the same rate would give ₹1,48,500.)

questions.q: Purchases during a month: 1st — 150 units @ ₹17; 10th — 100 units @ ₹21; 20th — 150 units @ ₹22. 250 units were issued on the 25th. Value of closing stock under FIFO is:
questions.x: Under FIFO the earliest units are issued first, so the 150 units left come from the latest purchases: 150 × ₹22 = ₹3,300.

questions.q: Government accounts in India are largely maintained on a:
questions.x: Union and State governments follow cash-based accounting; transition to accrual has been recommended.

questions.q: Outstanding expenses are shown in the balance sheet as:
questions.x: Correct answer: Current liabilities. They are amounts due but not paid.

questions.q: The cash book of a firm shows a debit (bank) balance of ₹80,000. Cheques issued but not yet presented: ₹3,000; cheques deposited but not yet credited: ₹5,500; bank charges debited only in the pass book: ₹50. The balance as per the pass book is:
questions.x:
Start with cash book balance ₹80,000.
+ Cheques issued not presented (bank has not yet paid) 3,000
− Cheques deposited not credited 5,500
− Bank charges 50
Pass book balance = ₹77,450.

questions.q: A high inventory turnover ratio generally indicates:
o: Efficient inventory management and fast-moving stock
questions.x: Correct answer: Efficient inventory management and fast-moving stock. However, an extremely high ratio may indicate stock-outs.

questions.q: A firm has Cash ₹15,000, Debtors ₹30,000, Inventory ₹80,000, Prepaid expenses ₹5,000, Creditors ₹20,000, Bills payable ₹2,500 and Outstanding expenses ₹5,000. Its current ratio is:

Consider the following statements:
1. Depreciation is a non-cash expense.
2. Depreciation provides funds for replacing assets in all cases.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is incorrect.
Depreciation does not by itself create a replacement fund unless profits are retained or a sinking fund is set up.

questions.q: Commission received in advance is adjusted by:
o: Cash A/c Dr. To Commission A/c
Commission A/c Dr. To Cash A/c
Commission Received in Advance A/c Dr. To Commission A/c
Commission A/c Dr. To Commission Received in Advance A/c
questions.x: Unearned income becomes a liability and reduces the current year's income.

questions.q: From the following, compute Gross Profit: Opening stock ₹40,000; Purchases ₹1,10,000; Purchase returns ₹4,000; Carriage inwards ₹1,000; Sales ₹1,42,000; Closing stock ₹70,000.
questions.x:
Cost of goods sold = Opening stock + Purchases − Purchase returns + Carriage inwards − Closing stock
= 40,000 + 1,10,000 − 4,000 + 1,000 − 70,000 = ₹77,000.
Gross profit = Net sales − COGS = 1,42,000 − 77,000 = ₹65,000.
Carriage inwards is a direct expense (Trading A/c).

questions.q: Ind AS were notified for phased implementation by companies beginning from the financial year:
questions.x: Phase I (listed and large companies with net worth ≥ ₹500 crore) applied from 1 April 2016.

questions.q: Consumer Price Index for Industrial Workers (CPI-IW), used to revise dearness allowance of central government employees, is compiled by:
o: Office of the Economic Adviser, DPIIT
questions.x: The Labour Bureau (Shimla/Chandigarh) compiles CPI-IW (base 2016 = 100) and CPI-AL/RL.

questions.q: The UK's Donovan Commission (1965–68) is known for its analysis of:
o: The two systems of industrial relations — formal national bargaining and informal workplace bargaining
questions.x: Donovan highlighted the gap between formal industry-wide agreements and informal shop-floor bargaining.

questions.q: 'Management by Objectives' (MBO) as an appraisal approach was popularised by:
questions.x: Correct answer: Peter Drucker. Drucker introduced MBO in 'The Practice of Management' (1954).

questions.q: Under the Code on Wages, monthly wages must be paid before the expiry of which day of the succeeding month?
questions.x: Section 17: for monthly wage periods, wages are payable before the expiry of the seventh day of the succeeding month.

questions.q: The Committee on Fair Wages (1948–49) distinguished three levels of wages. Arrange them in ascending order:
o: Fair wage < minimum wage < living wage
Minimum wage < living wage < fair wage
Minimum wage < fair wage < living wage
Living wage < fair wage < minimum wage
questions.x: The minimum wage is the floor for bare subsistence plus efficiency; the living wage is the ideal; the fair wage lies between them depending on capacity to pay.

questions.q:
Consider the following ILO fundamental conventions:
1. Convention No. 138 on Minimum Age
2. Convention No. 182 on Worst Forms of Child Labour
3. Convention No. 87 on Freedom of Association
Which of the above has India ratified?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is incorrect.
India ratified C138 and C182 in June 2017. India has not ratified C87 (and C98), mainly due to restrictions on government employees' rights.

questions.q: The recommendation to group India's labour laws into a few functional codes is most closely associated with which body?
o: Second National Commission on Labour (Ravindra Varma)
questions.x: The Second NCL (report 2002), chaired by Ravindra Varma, recommended rationalising central laws into broad codes such as wages, industrial relations, social security and safety.

questions.q: In T.K. Rangarajan v. Government of Tamil Nadu (2003), the Supreme Court held that:
o: Government employees have no fundamental, legal, moral or equitable right to go on strike
Strikes are a fundamental right under Article 21
Only private employees can be dismissed for striking
Government employees can strike without notice
questions.x: The judgment upheld the dismissal of striking Tamil Nadu government employees, while the government later reinstated most.

questions.q: The 'Worker Re-skilling Fund' under the IR Code is financed by the employer contributing, for each retrenched worker, an amount equal to:
questions.x: Section 83: the employer contributes 15 days' last drawn wages per retrenched worker; the amount is credited to the worker within 45 days of retrenchment.

questions.q: The Bombay Mill Hands Association (1890), regarded as the first organised labour association in India, was founded by:
questions.x: Narayan Meghaji Lokhande, a colleague of Jyotirao Phule, organised mill workers in Bombay and successfully demanded a weekly holiday.

questions.q: Under the OSH Code, a premises carrying on a manufacturing process WITHOUT the aid of power is a 'factory' if it employs at least:
questions.x: Without power, the factory threshold is 40 workers (earlier 20 under the Factories Act).

questions.q: In which year was the Payment of Bonus Act enacted?
questions.x: The Payment of Bonus Act was enacted in 1965.

questions.q: In the context of Indian labour law, 'protected workman' refers to:
o: A child worker rescued from hazardous work
A trade union office-bearer protected against change in service conditions during the pendency of proceedings
questions.x: Protected workmen are union office-bearers recognised as such; their service conditions cannot be altered or they cannot be dismissed during pendency of proceedings without permission.

questions.q: The 'pluralist' perspective of industrial relations holds that:
o: Conflict reflects class struggle that can end only with a new social order
Conflict between management and workers is natural and should be managed through institutions like collective bargaining
There is no conflict of interest in an organisation
questions.x: Pluralists (Oxford school — Flanders, Clegg, Fox) accept divergent interests and institutionalise conflict; the unitary view denies legitimate conflict; the Marxist view sees class conflict.

questions.q: Under the POSH Act, 2013, a complaint of sexual harassment should ordinarily be made within what period from the incident?
questions.x: A complaint is to be made within three months (extendable by another three months for valid reasons).

questions.q: Under the Aatmanirbhar Bharat Rojgar Yojana (ABRY), launched in October 2020, for establishments with up to 1,000 employees the Government paid:
o: Both employee and employer EPF contributions (24% of wages) for new employees for two years
A lump sum of ₹1 lakh per new employee
Only the employee's 12% for six months
questions.x: ABRY supported post-COVID job creation; for larger establishments only the employee share (12%) was paid. Registration closed in March 2022.

questions.q: Confinement expenses are paid under ESI when the delivery takes place:
o: At a place where necessary medical facilities under ESI are not available
In any private hospital by choice
questions.x: Confinement expenses are reimbursed if the delivery occurs where ESI facilities are not available.

questions.q: The Supreme Court in PUCL v. Union of India (the 'Right to Food' case, 2001 onwards) is known for:
o: Converting food schemes such as mid-day meals into legal entitlements through interim orders
questions.x: The Court's interim orders made mid-day meals and other schemes legal entitlements, paving the way for the NFSA.

questions.q: The 'replacement rate' of a pension scheme measures:
o: Number of pensioners replaced by new members
Pension as a percentage of pre-retirement earnings
questions.x: It indicates how well a pension maintains living standards after retirement.

questions.q: The rate of interest on EPF deposits is finalised by:
o: The Central Government on the recommendation of the CBT, in consultation with the Finance Ministry
questions.x: The CBT recommends the rate based on income; it is notified after the Ministry of Finance concurs.

questions.q: Widow/widower pension under EPS 1995 is payable at what share of the member's pension (subject to a minimum)?
questions.x: Widow pension is 50% of member pension, subject to a minimum of ₹1,000.

questions.q: The Unified Pension Scheme (UPS) for Central Government employees under NPS came into effect from:
questions.x: UPS was approved in August 2024 and notified in January 2025, effective 1 April 2025, as an option within NPS.

questions.q: An apprentice engaged under the Apprentices Act, 1961 is:
o: Covered only if the stipend exceeds ₹15,000
questions.x: Apprentices under the Apprentices Act or standing orders are excluded from the definition of employee.

questions.q: Under the maternity benefit law, a woman who has a miscarriage or medical termination of pregnancy is entitled to leave with wages for:
questions.x: Six weeks of paid leave is given immediately following the miscarriage or MTP.

questions.q: A woman employee entitled to 12 weeks of maternity benefit has an average daily wage of ₹680. Following the Supreme Court's view in B. Shah v. Presiding Officer (1977) that the benefit covers all days of the period, the total maternity benefit is:
questions.x:
The benefit is paid for every day of the 12-week period including Sundays: 12 × 7 = 84 days.
Amount = ₹680 × 84 = ₹57,120. (Using 6 days/week would wrongly give ₹48,960.)

questions.q: Which of the following is a statutory body for social security of unorganised workers under the Code on Social Security?
questions.x: The National Social Security Board recommends schemes and monitors welfare of unorganised, gig and platform workers.

questions.q: An insured employee earns gross wages of ₹14,500 in a month. What is the total ESI contribution (employer + employee) payable for that month?
questions.x:
Employee share 0.75% = ₹108.75 → ₹109; employer share 3.25% = ₹471.25 → ₹472 (rounded up to the next rupee).
Total = ₹581 (4% of wages; rates in force since 1 July 2019).

questions.q: Under MGNREGA, at least what share of beneficiaries should be women?
questions.x: The Act mandates that at least one-third of beneficiaries be women.

questions.q: A solar eclipse occurs when:
o: The Earth comes between the Sun and the Moon
The Moon comes between the Sun and the Earth
The Sun comes between the Earth and the Moon
questions.x: A lunar eclipse occurs when the Earth is between the Sun and the Moon (on a full moon).

questions.q: A 'database management system' (DBMS) is used to:
o: Store, retrieve and manage data efficiently
questions.x: Correct answer: Store, retrieve and manage data efficiently. MySQL, Oracle and PostgreSQL are examples.

questions.q: In computing, 'ASCII' stands for:
o: American Standard Code for Information Interchange
questions.x: ASCII = American Standard Code for Information Interchange.

questions.q: The unit 'kilowatt-hour' measures:
questions.x: Correct answer: Electrical energy. 1 kWh = 3.6 × 10⁶ J; it is the 'unit' on electricity bills.

questions.q: A device that forwards data packets between different networks is a:
questions.x: Correct answer: Router. A modem modulates/demodulates signals; a hub broadcasts to all ports.

questions.q: An alloy of copper and zinc is:
questions.x: Correct answer: Brass. Bronze is copper and tin; steel is iron with carbon.

questions.q: The binary equivalent of decimal 13 is:
Pernicious anaemia is caused by the deficiency of:
questions.x: Pernicious anaemia results from lack of Vitamin B12 (cobalamin).

questions.q: Bile, which emulsifies fats, is produced by the:
questions.x: Correct answer: Liver. It is stored in the gall bladder.

questions.q: 'Spam' refers to:
questions.x: Correct answer: Unsolicited bulk messages. Spam filters reduce it.

questions.q: Why are electric transmission wires allowed to sag?
o: To allow for contraction in winter
questions.x: Correct answer: To allow for contraction in winter. Metals contract in cold weather.

questions.q:
Consider the following:
Assertion (A): Diabetics are advised to limit sugar intake.
Reason (R): Their bodies cannot regulate blood glucose effectively due to lack of or resistance to insulin.
Select the correct answer:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
questions.x: Correct answer: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A. A is true and R is true; R correctly explains A. R explains A.

questions.q: A shopkeeper marks his goods 60% above the cost price and allows a discount of 15% on the marked price. His gain or loss per cent is:
questions.x:
Let CP = 100. Marked price = 160.
SP after 15% discount = 160 × 0.85 = 136.
Gain = 136 − 100 = 36 on 100 → 36% gain.
Shortcut: m − d − md/100 = 60 − 15 − 9 = 36%.

questions.q: In a line of trainees, Imran is 18th from the front and 6th from the back. How many persons are there in all?
questions.x: Total = (position from front) + (position from back) − 1 = 18 + 6 − 1 = 23. Imran is counted in both positions, hence −1.

questions.q: A sum of money lent at simple interest amounts to ₹5,500 in 2 years and to ₹6,250 in 5 years. The rate of interest per annum is:
In how many different ways can the letters of the word 'ACCOUNT' be arranged?
questions.x:
The word has 7 letters; C appears 2 times.
Arrangements = 7! / (2!) = 5,040 / 2 = 2,520.

questions.q: If 11 April of a certain year falls on a Sunday, on which day of the week will 3 December of the same year fall?
questions.x:
Days from 11 April to 3 December = 236 = 33 weeks + 5 odd days.
Sunday + 5 = Friday. (February is not involved, so leap years do not matter.)

questions.q: A vessel holds 40 litres of pure milk. 4 litres are drawn out and replaced with water. This operation is repeated once more. How much milk is now in the vessel?
questions.x:
After n replacements, milk = x(1 − y/x)ⁿ.
= 40 × (1 − 4/40)² = 40 × (0.9)² = 32.4 litres.
Removing 2 × 4 directly is wrong because the second draw removes a mixture, not pure milk.

questions.q:
Production of a fertiliser unit (thousand tonnes) — 2020: 140  |  2021: 200  |  2022: 175  |  2023: 175  |  2024: 170.
What is the percentage change from 2021 to 2024?
questions.x:
Change = 170 − 200 = -30 on a base of 200 (earlier year).
% change = -30/200 × 100 = -15% → 15% decrease.

questions.q: A train 400 m long running at 108 km/h crosses a platform in 26 seconds. The length of the platform is:
questions.x:
Speed = 108 × 5/18 = 30 m/s. Distance covered in 26 s = 780 m = train + platform.
Platform = 780 − 400 = 380 m.

questions.q: What is the least number which, when divided by 20, 18, 15, leaves a remainder of 2 in each case?
questions.x: Required number = LCM(20, 18, 15) + 2 = 180 + 2 = 182.

questions.q: Meena starts from point O and walks 8 km towards North, then turns left and walks 3 km, then turns left and walks 16 km, and finally turns right and walks 12 km. What is the shortest distance and direction of the final position from O?
questions.x:
Take O as origin, North/East positive.
North–South: +8 -16 = -8 km → 8 km South.
East–West: -3 -12 = -15 km → 15 km West.
Distance = √(15² + 8²) = 17 km, towards South-West.

questions.q: Two inlet pipes can fill a storage tank in 4 hours and 9 hours respectively, while an outlet pipe can empty the full tank in 36 hours. If all three are opened together on an empty tank, it will be full in:
questions.x:
Take tank capacity = LCM(4, 9, 36) = 36 units.
Rates: +9, +4, −1 units/hour → net 12 units/hour.
Time = 36 / 12 = 3 hours.

questions.q: Find the odd one out among 125, 1331, 998 and 1000.
questions.x: 1000, 125, 1331 are all perfect cubes; 998 is not. Hence 998 is the odd one out.

questions.q: Find the next term of the series: 20, 21, 25, 34, 50, ?
questions.x: Differences are 1², 2², 3², 4² (1, 4, 9, 16). Next difference = 5² = 25 → 50 + 25 = 75.

questions.q: a clerk and an assistant together can digitise a set of records in 28 days. a clerk alone can do it in 44 days. How many days will an assistant alone take?
questions.x:
an assistant's one-day work = 1/28 − 1/44 = (44 − 28)/1232 = 1/77.
So an assistant alone takes 77 days.
